title: Fallback orchestration decision graph for eviction and spillback
content:
Purpose
This is a working note that defines an orchestration-oriented decision graph for Greaceful Degradation during node/region capacity pressure, model eviction, or sudden regional outages. The goal is actionable runtime rules + a minimal control-plane protocol so the serving runtime can perform deterministic fallbacks with observable signals and safe defaults.

Scope and assumptions
- Applies to inference requests routed through the global control plane (hosted + dedicated).
- We assume model families have at least two compatible variants: a lower-cost (smaller/quantized) variant and a high-quality variant. Not all models have exact fallbacks; in those cases we rely on cached responses or rate limits.
- Customers have priority tiers: reserved (committed/Dedicated), standard (hosted paid), trial/free. Priority influences preemption, spillback acceptance, and throttling.
- Regional spillback here means: when a target region cannot accept traffic, the request is either routed to another region (spillover) or accepted by a local lower-tier capacity (spillback to tiered pool).

High-level decision graph (events -> actions)
1) Event: instance eviction or GPU OOM during request processing
   - Immediate runtime action: soft-fail request at the smallest safe boundary (return partial with header x-rdincomplete: true or retry)
   - Control-plane: mark instance as unstable, increment regional capacity-pressure counter, emit event CP:EV/eviction
   - Decision node: if model has in-region variant with kv-cache-compatible weights -> route to variant with KV cache transfer policy (see KV handoff below). Else follow fallback path 2.
2) Event: regional capacity pressure crosses threshold (5m spike > 70% reserved exhaustion)
   - Decision node: prioritize reserved customers; for standard/trial apply adaptive shedding: reduce max_tokens(default)-> tokens*0.7, switch sampler temp->0.45, or downgrade to smaller variant.
   - If cross-region latency budget allows (<200ms added), attempt spillover to nearest spare region with compatible model family. Otherwise, attempt local spillback to low-cost quantized pool.
3) Event: full region outage (health checks failed)
   - Control-plane action: flip route policy to forced spillover: tag affected AZ/region as UNAVAILABLE, notify routing mesh. Activate slow fallback TTL for active KV caches (60s) to avoid repeated cold starts.

Control-plane responsibilities (minimal contract)
- Signal types (simple and versioned): REGION_PRESSURE, INSTANCE_EVICT, MODEL_DEGRADE, SPILLOVER_DECISION, SPILLBACK_DECISION. Each event includes: affected_region, model_family, priority_impact, timestamp, suggested_variant_id.
- Decisions are recommendations but contain a policyIntent object: {target_variant, max_tokens_multiplier, preserve_kv_cache_bool, allow_spillover_regions}. Runtime may override when local metrics contradict control-plane signal.
- Control-plane keeps a short-lived decision token (idempotent decision_id) valid for N seconds (default 30s). Runtimes attach decision_id to follow-up requests for traceability.

Runtime responsibilities and heuristics
- Local fast-path: on eviction or OOM, runtime should attempt up to 2 quick automatic retries within same instance class (0-200ms backoff) before consulting the control-plane. This avoids control-plane thrash for transient glitches.
- KV cache handoff heuristic: allow in-memory KV transfer only between sibling variant binaries when model_family and kv_schema match exactly. Otherwise, persist prefix cache to quickstore for 30s and allow hot-read by fallback variant.
- Latency SLO preservation: for latency-sensitive routes (route.metadata.latency_slo_ms <= 50ms), prefer local degraded features (reduce tokens, sampling tweak) over cross-region spillover. For throughput routes prefer spillover.

Tiered capacity and preemption rules
- Pools: reserved_pool (guaranteed), burst_pool (on-demand paid), spot_pool (cheaper but preemptible), quantized_pool (smaller/low-RMSE variants).
- Preemption: when reserved_pool is underutilized we never preempt. When reserved_pool exhausted, control-plane signals preemption order: spot_pool -> burst_pool -> quantized_pool. However preemption is per-customer policy: customers with reserved contracts may be allowed to preempt burst/spot owned by others.
- Fairness tokens: assign short-lived fairness tokens per user/tenant when under load; tokens decrement after each downgrade. If tokens==0, the tenant receives either HTTP 429 or a mandatory variant downgrade.

Spillback vs spillover decision matrix (simple)
- If latency_addition_due_to_spillover < route.max_extra_latency -> choose SPILLOVER (to keep quality)
- Else if compatible quantized_variant exists AND model_deviation_metric < threshold -> choose SPILLBACK (local downgrade)
- Else if cached response exists with recency < cache_ttl -> return cached (best-effort)

Operational playbook (incident steps)
- Detect: regional sentinel triggers REGION_PRESSURE for 2 consecutive 1-min windows.
- Triage: on-call inspects the decision graph state in Control UI -> shows pending decision_ids, affected pools, and list of currently routed requests.
- Mitigate: toggle surge-mode: enforce conservative shedding rules for non-critical tenants (apply max_tokens*0.6 and sampling temperature 0.4) and allow spillover for reserved customers.
- Observe: verify fallback quality by sampling responses from fallback variants and running quick-eval (bleu/semantic-similarity) on a small golden set. Reverse decision if quality unacceptable.

Telemetry and SLOs to make decisions safe
- Required metrics: per-region free_gpu_pct, avg_queue_time_ms, active_model_instances, cache_hit_rate, fallback_rate_by_variant, p50/p95 latency per route+variant, quality_regression_signal (eval-based), token_cost_delta.
- Alerting: fallback_rate > 5% for 10m -> pages platform oncall. region_free_gpu_pct < 8% -> pages infra.

Policy DSL (example snippet - plaintext)
# policyId: regretless-1
route: \/v1/generate
priority_map: {
  reserved: 100,
  standard: 50,
  free: 10
}
rules:
  - when: region.free_gpu_pct < 15
    then:
      - action: reduce_tokens
        multiplier: 0.7
      - action: prefer_spillover_if
        latency_budget_ms: 150
  - when: instance.evictions_1m > 3
    then:
      - action: restrict_to_variant
        variant_tag: quantized-kv-compatible
      - action: emit_metric
        name: runtime_restricted_variant

Decision graph examples (concrete flows)
1) Busy period, US-WEST nearing reserved exhaustion: burst_pool available in us-east
   - Control-plane calculates spillover_latency = 120ms, route.max_extra_latency = 100ms -> choose spillback (downgrade to quantized pool). Reserved tenants remain on full model and are routed cross-region.
2) Node evicted mid-request, KV cache transferable -> runtime attaches decision_id, transfers small prefix cache, retries on sibling variant within 50ms, request succeeds, control-plane logs EV/repair event.
3) Full region outage -> control-plane sets UNAVAILABLE; per-route policy TTL for KV caches extended to 60s to enable faster cold starts in failover region.

Testing and cutover plan
- Canary test: enable policy with canary tag for 5% of traffic to a non-critical route; watch fallback_rate and quality_regression.
- Load test: synthetic spike that simulates 3x reserved usage for 10m. Validate fair token distribution and preemption order.
- Chaos experiment: kill x% of nodes in region during test window and ensure decision flow routes requests with decision tokens and no infinite loops.

Open questions / TODOs
- How to represent model-family compatibility more granularly? (semantic vs binary-compatibility).
- Improve KV handoff for heterogeneous quantization formats (4-bit -> 8-bit). Research persistence approach and latency cost.
- Define exact fairness token decay curve and how it interacts with multi-route tenants.
- Add cross-tenant spillover quota to avoid a single large tenant consuming spare region capacity.

Appendix: quick checklist for oncall
- Verify control-plane event stream contains decision_id for affected requests.
- Check top 5 tenants by downgraded requests. If a single tenant dominates, consider manual soft-limit.
- Run quick eval on sample of downgraded responses (automated script path: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/tools/fallback-eval).
- If degradation persists > 15m, escalate to platform lead and open an incident PI for capacity planning.

Notes to reviewers
- This doc is intentionally prescriptive but lightweight. Looking for feedback on decision token TTL and fairness token algorithm. Also want validation from infra on practical preemption ordering between burst and spot pools.
- Ping: @Ethan Cole for KV handoff feasibility, @Priya Nair for SLO heuristics, @Jamal Ortiz for incident playbook wording.

History: initial draft 2025-02-18 by Marta A.; edits 2025-03-02 (added API of decision token + example DSL).
